**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "malty, full-bodied black tea that stands up to milk" | Product/flavour fact, fine |
| "boosts your immunity through winter" | Unsupported. Health claim, never allowed (policy §3) |
| "Certified organic by the Soil Association" | Allowlisted, exact wording |
| "100g tin, makes around 40 cups" | Product fact (tin size and cup count), fine |

**Voice check:** No banned words, no em-dashes, no exclamation marks, no rhetorical opener. The copy is plain and short. UK spelling is fine.

**Problem:** "boosts your immunity through winter" is a health claim. It also has no proof, and it would likely breach UK advertising rules on health claims for food and drink. It must come out.

**Suggested fix (compliant version):**

> Assam Breakfast. A malty, full-bodied black tea that stands up to milk. Good for dark mornings and a splash of milk in winter. Certified organic by the Soil Association. 100g tin, makes around 40 cups.

If you'd prefer something tighter, just drop the sentence:

> Assam Breakfast. A malty, full-bodied black tea that stands up to milk. Certified organic by the Soil Association. 100g tin, makes around 40 cups.

Either version needs Sam's sign-off before it goes live, as all public content does.
